name: ESSAI 2026
venue: European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence, Vienna, Austria
description: The 2026 European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence (ESSAI) takes place in Vienna, Austria, from 6 to 10 July. It provides a one‑week intensive program of introductory and advanced AI courses, tutorials, and tracks covering topics such as Bilateral AI and Digital Humanism, aimed at PhD students, young researchers, and senior scholars. The school also features networking opportunities, social events, and is co‑located with the 5th ACM Europe Digital Humanism Summer School.

name: OpenEuroLLM Winter School
venue: Skeikampen conference hotel, near Oslo, Norway
description: The 2026 Winter School on Multilinguality in LLM Development and Evaluation is organized by the Nordic Language Processing Laboratory and held at the Skeikampen conference hotel north of Oslo, Norway. It targets NLP researchers, especially those from EuroHPC consortium countries and doctoral students, offering technical presentations, hands‑on elements, and discussions on multilingual large language models and evaluation. The program includes expert talks, bus transfers from Oslo Airport, and is subsidized by the OpenEuroLLM project, with no registration fee but participants covering travel and accommodation costs.

name: Probabilistic AI School
description: The ProbAI School 2026 is a Probabilistic AI School taking place in Vilnius, Lithuania. It aims to provide an inclusive educational environment covering state‑of‑the‑art machine‑learning and artificial‑intelligence topics for enthusiasts, students, academics and industry professionals. The event is co‑organized with the Artificial Intelligence Association of Lithuania (AIAL).

name: BMVA Computer Vision Summer School
description: The 29th BMVA Computer Vision Summer School will be held at Durham University in Durham, England, UK. It offers an intensive week of lectures and lab sessions covering a wide range of topics in computer vision, delivered by leading researchers from the UK and abroad. The programme features daily oral talks and hands‑on sessions designed to provide participants with deep, practical knowledge of current computer‑vision methods.

name: Oxford Machine Learning Summer School 2026
venue: Oxford Machine Learning School, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: The Summer 2026 Oxford Machine Learning School (OxML) offers a three‑track programme that can be taken in Oxford or online. It brings together world‑renowned experts from leading AI labs in academia and industry, allowing participants to customise their learning by selecting any combination of tracks. The school aims to upskill attendees in the latest AI theory and applications while fostering a global community of researchers, practitioners, and innovators.

name: Robotics, Perception and Learning (RPL) Summer School
venue: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden
description: The RPL Summer School 2026 is a six‑day event for doctoral and postdoctoral researchers organized by the Department for Robotics, Perception and Learning at KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm, Sweden. It covers a broad spectrum of topics such as machine learning, computer vision, robotics, human‑robot interaction, planning and decision making, combining keynote talks, industry panels and brainstorming sessions to foster new collaborations. The program includes student presentations, indoor and outdoor ice‑breaker activities, and is hosted at the Happy Tammsvik resort with accommodation, meals and materials provided by the organizers.

name: Machine Learning Crash Course at MALGA
description: The MLCC2026 Summer School – Machine Learning Crash Course – provides an introduction to fundamental machine‑learning concepts and algorithms. It is aimed at undergraduate and graduate students, as well as professionals, and is open to participants from any university after a selection process. The five‑day in‑person program in Genoa combines theoretical lectures with hands‑on lab sessions and includes a final test consisting of notebook work and a report.

name: UK Robotics Summer School
venue: National Robotarium, Heriot-Watt University, Edinburgh, United Kingdom
description: The UK Robotics Summer School 2026 is a five‑day event held at the National Robotarium, Heriot‑Watt University in Edinburgh, United Kingdom. It offers expert‑led lectures, tutorials and industry talks covering bio‑inspired robotics, healthcare robotics, generative AI, safe AI and real‑world applications, with hands‑on experience using state‑of‑the‑art technology. The programme targets master’s‑level students and industry practitioners, providing networking opportunities with academics and industry leaders.

name: International Summer School for Advanced Studies on Biometrics, Behavior, and Vision
description: The 2026 Biometrics Summer School takes place in Alghero, Sardinia, Italy, hosted at the Hotel Dei Pini. It focuses on the impact of generative AI and large foundation models on biometric and human‑recognition technologies, covering machine learning, image understanding, signal analysis, neuroscience, robotics, forensic and digital forensics. The program is aimed at PhD students, post‑docs, researchers and professionals such as forensic examiners and police officers, offering intensive lectures by 20 international experts, hands‑on sessions, and optional videoconference participation.

name: Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal (ELS) aspects of AI and AS at Umeå University
description: The Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal aspects of AI and Autonomous Systems brings together researchers and students to explore the broader implications of emerging technologies. It offers a mix of lectures, hands‑on multidisciplinary training, a poster session, and a social program to foster networking and professional exchange. The event takes place at Umeå University in Sweden from 11 to 13 March 2026.

name: Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia (SoRAIM 2026)
description: The ACM Europe Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia (SoRAIM’27) will be held in early February 2027 in the Vercors mountains near Grenoble. It targets PhD students and early‑career researchers, offering lectures, hands‑on sessions and informal networking on topics such as computer vision, speech processing, affective computing and human‑robot interaction. The mountain setting provides opportunities for outdoor activities and fosters cross‑disciplinary collaboration among academia and industry participants.

name: Northern Lights Deep Learning Winter School
venue: UiT The Arctic University of Norway, Tromsø, Norway
description: The 2027 Northern Lights Deep Learning Winter School is part of the NLDL conference in Tromsø, Norway. It runs from 11 to 15 January 2027 and focuses on deep learning topics such as image classification, object detection, segmentation, time‑series prediction and speech recognition. The school brings together researchers and practitioners to exchange ideas, foster collaborations, and learn from leading experts in the field.

name: Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS)
description: The 7th Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS) is an intensive 11‑day program held at Kathmandu World School in Kathmandu, Nepal. It offers lectures, hands‑on labs, and project work covering AI fundamentals and advanced topics such as geometric deep learning, world models, generative modeling, and neuro‑symbolic AI. The school targets senior undergraduates, graduate students, PhD candidates, faculty, and industry professionals from Nepal and abroad.

name: EEML Summer School
description: The Eastern European Machine Learning Summer School takes place in Cetinje, Montenegro from 27 July to 1 August 2026. It offers an intensive program of lectures and tutorials on machine‑learning research presented by leading experts from academia and industry. The school targets graduate students and early‑career researchers from the region and provides networking opportunities with sponsors such as Google DeepMind and other partners.

name: Mediterranean Summer School
description: The Mediterranean Machine Learning (M2L) Summer School is a five‑day intensive program that brings together early‑stage researchers and experts to present keynotes, lectures and hands‑on sessions on modern AI topics. It targets doctoral and outstanding master students, as well as academics and practitioners, especially from the Mediterranean region, and encourages participants to showcase their work in poster sessions and to network through social activities. The school covers a broad range of subjects such as computer vision, natural language processing, generative models, reinforcement learning, applied deep learning, neuroscience and ethics in machine learning.

name: Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI
venue: Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications, Rabat, Morocco
description: The 2nd edition of the AI Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI is a five‑day immersive program held at the Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications in Rabat, Morocco. It offers young researchers, Ph.D. and master students, post‑docs, and industry professionals a mix of theoretical lectures, hands‑on labs, and networking events to explore state‑of‑the‑art multimodal and generative AI techniques. The school is jointly organized by MoroccoAI, INPT, IMT Nord Europe and Soft Centre, providing participants access to world‑renowned experts and fostering the next generation of AI leaders in Morocco.

name: AthNLP Summer School 2026
description: The Athens Natural Language Processing Summer School 2026 is hosted at the NCSR Demokritos campus in Athens, Greece. It offers a week-long program (September 2‑8) focusing on recent advances and research in natural language processing, with lectures and hands‑on sessions. The school is jointly organized by several research institutes and universities, and it coincides with the 14th EETN Conference on Artificial Intelligence.

name: Advanced Artificial Intelligence: GenAI & Deep Unsupervised Learning
venue: Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: The Advanced Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning summer school at Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, focuses on generative AI and deep unsupervised learning techniques. It offers theoretical instruction and hands‑on experience with topics such as clustering, GANs, self‑supervised learning, anomaly detection, and unsupervised reinforcement learning, targeting STEM students with intermediate AI knowledge. The intensive residential (or online) program runs from 29 June to 17 July 2026 and aims to provide career‑relevant skills and a foundation for future research.

name: AI4Science Summer School
description: The 2nd Summer School on Advancing Scientific Discovery with AI takes place in Caen, Normandy, France in 2025. It focuses on applying AI techniques such as machine learning, generative models, and AI‑driven experimental design to accelerate scientific research across various domains. The program targets PhD students, post‑doctoral researchers and scientists, offering hands‑on workshops and case studies using Python libraries like NumPy and PyTorch.

name: LUT Summer School
description: LUT Summer School 2026 is a one‑week intensive programme at LUT University’s Lappeenranta campus offering courses on sustainability, climate action, marketing, management and the intersection of business and technology. The school is aimed at bachelor’s and master’s students from any university who wish to earn 3 ECTS credits while engaging in workshops, group projects and hands‑on learning. Participants also benefit from a social programme that includes Finnish‑style sauna evenings, outdoor activities and the opportunity to experience the Finnish summer in Lappeenranta.

name: 1st Internationa School on the Cognitive, Ethical, and Societal Dimensions of AI - AIces
description: AIces 2026 is the first International School on the Cognitive, Ethical and Societal Dimensions of Artificial Intelligence, held in Porto, Portugal from 30 March to 2 April 2026. The program offers parallel courses, a symposium with short presentations, and open‑debate sessions, allowing graduate students, post‑graduates and industry practitioners to explore multidisciplinary discussions on AI foundations, challenges and risks. Participants can attend face‑to‑face or live online, receive recorded lectures for 45 days, and obtain a certificate that may be used for ECTS recognition.
